Current Work

Projects we're actively pursuing. Each addresses a specific gap in the AI safety and governance landscape.

In Progress

Interpretability Research Fund

Status Scoping & funder conversations
Target launch Q1 2027
Budget range $50k–$200k initial

Problem

Mechanistic interpretability—understanding what neural networks are actually doing internally—is one of the most promising paths to scalable alignment. But funding is fragmented, and many promising directions (sparse autoencoders, activation patching, automated interpretability) lack sustained support.

Approach

A small, nimble fund making 6–12 month grants ($10k–$50k) to researchers pursuing interpretability directions that could scale to superhuman systems. Prioritizing: (1) methods that don't require human inspection of every feature, (2) work on larger models (>10B params), (3) cross-model generalization of interpretability techniques.

Current needs

  • Committed funders (targeting 3–5 anchor donors)
  • Technical advisory board (3–5 researchers)
  • Grant administration infrastructure
Get involved →

AI Governance Primer for Policymakers

Status Drafting v0.3
Target release January 2027
Format 20-page PDF + interactive site

Problem

Policymakers and staff need a single, non-technical document that maps the governance landscape: compute governance, liability regimes, international agreements, licensing, incident reporting, and institutional design. Existing resources are either too academic, too lab-centric, or too vague.

Approach

A concise briefing structured around decision points: "If you want to achieve X, here are the policy levers, their trade-offs, and where the expert consensus lies." Each section includes a one-page summary, a deeper dive, and annotated references. Reviewed by governance researchers and former staffers before publication.

  • Reviewers with policy experience (targeting 5–8)
  • Design/layouts for PDF and web versions
  • Distribution strategy (Hill offices, EU Parliament, UN, national AI institutes)

Problem

Many talented researchers in adjacent fields (ML theory, neuroscience, physics, control theory, formal verification) want to contribute to alignment but face high switching costs: unfamiliar literature, unclear research problems, lack of mentorship, funding gaps during transition.

Approach

A 6-month fellowship providing: stipend ($30k–$50k), mentorship pairing with senior alignment researchers, structured curriculum (reading groups, problem formulation workshops), compute credits, and a cohort community. Targeting researchers 0–5 years post-PhD or equivalent industry experience.
